human_tolerance.notes: Uses gardens and other suitable built-area habitats where basking sites, dense cover and prey are present.

taxonomy.note: GBIF resolves accepted species rank and canonical name; its API places Squamata in the class field and omits an order. ITIS independently resolves accepted species TSN 1155342 with standard hierarchy Reptilia (class), Squamata (order), Lacertidae, Zootoca; that hierarchy is used here.

external.note: GBIF usage key 9702100 resolves accepted species; Wikidata P3151 and iNaturalist API independently give taxon ID 35453 at species rank; ITIS TSN 1155342 resolves accepted species.

range.note: Record is scoped to issue region GB; species is native in the British Isles. The wider distribution is omitted.

traits.limb_count.note: Four-limbed lizard; species schema counts walking limbs.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Ground-dwelling lizard; Walk represents ordinary ground locomotion. The kit has no run gait.

traits.nest_type.note: Live-bearing species; no nest structure represented.

traits.size_class.note: Tiny from adult male/female mean mass, 3.64 g, below the schema 50 g boundary.

traits.mass_kg.note: Average of study population adult male mean 3.43 g and female mean 3.85 g = 3.64 g. Population was southwestern Poland; this is the best measured adult proxy found, not a range-wide estimate.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: Combines reported adult male BW range 1.2-6.0 g (N=73) and adult female range 1.2-7.6 g (N=61), converted to kg; excludes juveniles and lizards with autotomized/regrown tails.

traits.length_m.note: Total length derived from adult means in Table 1: male SVL 48.1 mm + TL 80.2 mm = 128.3 mm; female SVL 53.9 mm + TL 77.9 mm = 131.8 mm; midpoint of the two sex means = 130.05 mm, rounded to 0.13 m. Data are one southwestern Poland population; autotomy/regrown-tail animals were excluded from tail samples.

traits.lifespan_y.note: ADW Lifespan/Longevity says average wild lifespan 5 to 6 years; value is midpoint (5+6)/2 = 5.5 years. The same section separately reports wild high 8 years and captive typical 4 to 6 years; neither is substituted. Wikipedia repeats 5-6 years without stating wild/captive scope, so it does not replace this explicit wild statistic; All Angles Creatures summarizes a 2.8-year average without resolving population scope, so it is not treated as a range-wide typical estimate.

traits.diet.note: Invertebrates are the stated diet; 100% is an authored single-category allocation because the schema requires diet shares to sum to one.

traits.social.note: Solitary is the conservative simulation representation; ADW describes both solitary and small-group populations. Group size represents a single individual.

traits.defense.note: Rapid escape to cover is the documented response.

traits.wariness.note: Authored judgement based on described timid, quick escape behavior.

habitat.use.note: Ground use assigned 1.0 because the animal is terricolous; categorical allocation.

habitat.resources.note: Invertebrate prey and dense-cover/leaf-litter refuge represented; weights are authored relative importance.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Gardens are reported habitat; tolerance category is a simulation judgement.

seasonal.note: Date window reflects ADW-reported mid-October to mid-March brumation. Trigger thresholds are an authored simulation judgement because this source gives dates rather than a temperature trigger.

behavior.note: Species-local FSM uses Walk for ordinary and escape movement; it temperature- and day-gates activity, enters shelter when conditions turn cold or dark, and limits active-month behavior to March-October. The kit has no bask action, so basking is approximated by rest during warm daylight. Thresholds and flee distances are authored simulation judgements.

look.note: Color and long-tailed proportions are generalized from variable brown/green body, darker dorsal pattern, pale/yellow-orange underside; block proportions are rendering judgement.
